row.description: ISBN-13 is the book-identification convention defined by ISO 2108. This profile uses the visible 3-1-4-4-1 hyphenation layout. A wrong generalization would treat hyphens as optional decoration or accept any 13-digit number without validating the ISBN-13 check digit and registration-group structure.

neighbors.distinction: ISSN identifies serial publications and has eight digits rather than the ISBN-13 book identifier layout.
A DOI is a resolver-oriented identifier with slash-separated registrant syntax rather than an ISBN registration-group pattern.

concept: ASME drawing number with optional revision suffix

row.concept: ASME drawing number with optional revision suffix
row.description: Technical-drawing control commonly uses an ASME Y14.100-style drawing identifier with a revision letter for a revised issue; an initial issue may omit the revision suffix. A wrong generalization would require a revision for every drawing, accept numeric revision marks in a letter-only workflow, or treat the revision as part of the immutable drawing number.

neighbors.distinction: An issue date records publication time, whereas the revision suffix identifies a controlled revision state.
An ECO authorizes a change; it is not the revision identifier printed on the drawing.

row.description: PDF print and export dialogs conventionally express selected page intervals as comma-separated inclusive ranges, for example 1-3,5-7. A wrong generalization would treat the field as unrestricted prose, allow a bare page number when this range-only profile is expected, or accept typographic dashes that a machine parser does not recognize as range separators.

neighbors.distinction: A single page reference names one page, while this profile requires explicit start-end range sections.
A bookmark destination is a navigational target rather than a print-selection interval list.

row.description: A classic PDF cross-reference-table entry stores its byte offset as a zero-padded decimal field with exactly ten digits before the generation-number field. The apparent fixed width in samples is normative for the classic xref-table syntax, not evidence that offsets are ordinary variable-width integers. A wrong generalization would strip leading zeros or accept shorter offsets without padding.

neighbors.distinction: The generation number is a bounded object-version counter, while this field is a byte position in the PDF file.
A stream length is ordinarily represented as an integer object and is not constrained to the classic xref ten-character field width.
